vulnerability.category_l2: SQL injection through the clear() prefix: the value is concatenated into a LIKE literal in PdoAdapter::doClear() and executed without binding or escaping

critical_operation.description: AbstractAdapterTrait::clear($prefix) computes $namespaceToClear = $this->namespace.$prefix when versioning is disabled and passes it to PdoAdapter::doClear(). For a non-empty namespace, doClear() builds "DELETE FROM <table> WHERE <id_col> LIKE '<namespace>%'" by string interpolation and runs it with PDO::exec(); the value is never bound or quoted. A prefix containing a single quote can close the LIKE literal and reshape or widen the DELETE, and % wildcards or other SQL syntax reach the statement as well. The 5.4.52 fix validates the prefix in AbstractAdapterTrait::clear() against [-+.A-Za-z0-9] and returns false before doClear() is reached; PdoAdapter.php itself is unchanged.

entry_point.description: Application code calls clear($prefix) on a PdoAdapter-backed pool with a prefix that comes from a request or another untrusted source. The method is public and documented to accept an arbitrary prefix, although most applications do not expose it directly.

supports: doClear(string $namespace) builds "DELETE FROM $this->table WHERE $this->idCol LIKE '$namespace%'" for a non-empty namespace at line 435
the string is interpolated directly and passed to $conn->exec($sql) at line 439; there is no prepared statement or quote() call

clear(string $prefix = "") computes $namespaceToClear = $this->namespace.$prefix in the non-versioning branch (line 147)
it passes that value to $this->doClear() without validating the prefix
the versioning branch uses the stored namespace version instead, so the vulnerable path requires versioning to be disabled
PdoAdapter.php is byte-identical at v5.4.52; the SQL construction is unchanged
the fix is applied upstream in AbstractAdapterTrait::clear(), so the sink receives only validated prefixes

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on CWE-89, the unbound prefix in doClear(), the <5.4.52 range, the v5.4.52 release and fix commit ec50b799. NVD publishes a Primary CVSS 3.1 7.3 HIGH and a Secondary CVSS 4.0 6.3 MEDIUM; the GHSA MODERATE label matches the 4.0 score but not the 3.1 score. The fix is in AbstractAdapterTrait::clear() rather than in PdoAdapter.php, so the sink file is byte-identical at both tags.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read PdoAdapter::doClear at v5.4.45 and confirm the LIKE literal is built by interpolation and run with exec().
An independent reviewer must read AbstractAdapterTrait::clear at v5.4.45 and confirm the prefix is not validated on the non-versioning path.
An independent reviewer must confirm ec50b799 is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.52, and that the fix validates the prefix in the trait while leaving PdoAdapter.php unchanged.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.52.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No database, PDO connection or SQL payload was executed; the finding is static.
Reachability requires application code to pass an untrusted prefix to clear(); the advisory itself notes most applications do not expose it.
The versioning path does not use the prefix, so the issue applies only when versioning is disabled.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; 6.4.40, 7.4.12 and 8.0.12 were not diffed.
NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 7.3 High and CNA CVSS 4.0 6.3 Medium disagree materially.
open_questions: Whether other adapters (DoctrineDbalAdapter and friends) share the same unvalidated prefix path was not audited.
Which Symfony applications expose clear($prefix) to request data was not surveyed.
